Subject: Telemetry trials & competitor checks — proposed next steps

Hi Elaine / Tom,

Thanks again for the time earlier — really appreciate how specific you were about the telemetry and routing concerns. Short recap + proposed next steps so we can align on scope for the trial: 

Recap (from the demo)
- You want token-level latency breakdowns, per-route QPS/latency dashboards, and visibility into KV-cache utilization for prefix-heavy workloads.
- Primary business questions: how Redwood compares to hyperscaler endpoints (cost/latency under sustained traffic), and whether our smart routing/fallback behavior affects observability.
- Data residency/log retention constraints: logs must remain in the US region and be retained for 90 days for audit.

Proposed telemetry trial (1 week) — goals
1) Verify token-latency and tail latency at 95/99p for your steady-state workload.
2) Compare trace fidelity and attribution vs two hyperscaler endpoints (A = Bedrock-like, B = Vertex-like) using the same client traffic generator.
3) Validate dashboarding (Drilldown to model version, route, and token bucket) and integrations (Datadog).

What we need from you to start
- Confirm 1-week window (we proposed Mar 8–14) — are you available?
- Share representative prompt set + estimated QPS pattern (attachment: telemetry-test-plan.xlsx has a template).
- Point-of-contact for infra access / whitelist (for load generator IPs).

Internal notes: I copied Marissa to scope instrumentation and Sergio for commercial alignment.

If that works, I’ll kick off the test plan, loop in Ben for the benchmark harness, and share a Drive folder with live dashboards.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Hi Elaine/Tom — jumping in with a technical outline and two concrete tests we can run during the week-long trial. I kept it pragmatic so we can produce apples-to-apples results vs the hyperscalers.

Summary of what Redwood can surface
- Token-level latency (per-token timings emitted from the runtime).
- KV cache hit/miss metrics exposed per-model-version and per-route.
- Trace propagation with full span trees (request -> routing -> model-inference -> postprocess) so you can see whether fallback or regional failover collapses span attribution.
- Integration hooks: Datadog (APM + Metrics), S3-compatible log export with configurable retention, and optional redaction transforms.

Comparative test matrix (Redwood vs Hyperscaler A vs Hyperscaler B) — key axes- Sampling fidelity: raw spans vs sampled traces- Token timing resolution: 1ms vs 5ms vs 10ms- Visibility into cache state: per-key metrics or aggregate only- End-to-end trace continuity across routing/fallback- Dashboard drilldown latency (time-to-first-update)

Proposed tests
1) Sustained-concurrency A/B run (3h window x 3 runs)
- Load: 200 QPS steady + 2 spikes to 1k QPS for 30s
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tail amplification during spike, and how quickly KV cache warms under short prompts.
- Expectation: Redwood’s continuous batching + KV visibility should produce lower cost-per-token and clearer cache metrics.

2) Prefix-replay & routing-fallback test
- Scenario: 30% prefix repetition, route some traffic to a degraded region to force routing fallback.
- Measure: trace continuity (do spans from origin survive routing?), attribution correctness, and dashboard reconciliation (do counts match raw logs).

Deliverables we’ll provide during the trial- Live dashboards (Datadog) scoped to your account and filters for route/model/version. (screenshot-dashboard.png attached)- A CSV of the comparison metrics and raw traces (redwood-telemetry-comparison-metrics.csv).

Notes on PII redaction
- We’ll enable a pre-ingest redaction transform for any fields you flag as sensitive. Raw traces used for debugging will be available under a restricted role for 90 days, per your retention requirement.

Next steps from Redwood engineering
- Ben will stand up the harness and ensure the load generator uses identical request patterns across providers.
- I’ll prepare the Datadog dashboards and share the Drive folder before EOD Friday.

If that aligns, I’ll post the dashboard link and the CSV after we complete the first run.

--
Marissa Cole
